meta.tagline: What downtown Providence has, what it does not, and how long the missing take to grow.
meta.disclosure: Every row in the ledger is on it because a peer downtown has the thing or the city itself has proposed it, never because the author thinks a downtown ought to. Every judgment about a walk is one person's estimate of what a typical pedestrian would do, recorded the same way each time, with a reason on every no.

items.name: Daytime workers inside
items.where: About 15,000 jobs inside the Downcity overlay in 2023 (14,975; 15,211 in 2022; 13,852 in 2019), about 140 per acre over 107 acres. Largest sectors: professional services 2,751, food and lodging 2,345, finance and insurance 2,087. Retail is 152. The wider city 'Downtown' neighborhood has 26,491, down 9% from 2019's 29,141. These are jobs sited at an employer address, not people in the building on a given day; LODES does not see remote work.

new-haven.note: About 11,100 jobs in 2023 (11,111; 10,940 in 2019), about 77 per acre over 145 acres, Town Green District drawn to street centrelines from the district's own map.

items.notes: Counted Sept 28 2026 with lodes.py: 2020 census blocks whose internal point falls inside each polygon, all jobs (S000, JT00). Providence's line is the zoning overlay (parcel-edged); the peers' are street centrelines, so their acreage includes half the boundary streets. Block-level siting is noisy: two neighbouring blocks on either side of the Downcity line swapped about 850 jobs between 2019 and 2023. Polygons in data/geo/peers/. The demand root the clock runs on.

items.name: Office vacancy
items.where: Downtown-specific: more than 20% of commercial space empty in the Financial District and nearly 32% in Capital Center, per the Boston Globe in April 2025. Q4 2021 was 15.85% for downtown per CBRE, the last published downtown-only rate. Market-wide: 13.7% overall vacancy, all classes, Q2 2026, per Cushman & Wakefield and Hayes & Sherry's Providence MarketBeat; year-to-date net absorption 115,000 sq ft; asking rent $23.03. The report says the market is tight with no speculative office construction expected, and that FM's purchase of 10 Memorial Blvd took nearly 60,000 sq ft of Class A space off the central business district.

worcester.note: Two marketing posts five days apart give Class A at about 14% vacant (Mar 4 2026) and about 10% (Mar 9 2026); Worcester market, Class A only, no dated quarterly report.

new-haven.note: 19.7% availability, H1 2025, New Haven County per CBRE; availability rather than vacancy, county rather than downtown. 24.26% all-class market figure in 2024 per CommercialCafe.

items.notes: The MarketBeat has no CBD line: its only submarket breakdown is a map key, and Providence is one submarket, the whole city (read Sept 28 2026). Downtown-only figures since 2021 are the Globe's two district numbers; no firm publishes a quarterly downtown rate for Providence in the open. Peers are market-wide.

items.name: RIPTA transit center relocation
items.where: On August 20, 2026 RIPTA's board voted 6 to 0 to take a new transit center into design, engineering and pricing on a 4.4-acre state-owned parcel facing Francis and Gaspee streets, next to Providence Station and across from Providence Place. Contractor Next Wave Partners. Kennedy Plaza would keep reduced service via the Downtown Transit Connector. The governor's schematic shows 16 bus berths curving along the Francis and Gaspee intersection, west of the station and south of the State House. RIPTA will own the site; it is a tenant at Kennedy Plaza, which the City owns. Next Wave's contract is about $16.9 million. The board packet puts the preliminary estimate at $70 million, not final, against $77 million committed ($46 million in the state transportation plan, a $25 million federal BUILD grant, $6 million state match), and says construction would begin within six months of finishing the design contract. No date is given for finishing it; the design and a cost estimate come back to the board first. RIDOT's station page still says 2026 for the station work next door, with no completion announced as of Sept 28.

needs.text: Design, engineering, pricing, public engagement and permitting complete, and the proposal with a cost estimate returns to the board for approval; no date stated
Funding assembled: 2014 transit bond share plus a $25M federal BUILD grant, with state documents describing the bond figures differently ($20.5M recommended, $22M issued)
Route restructuring settled: which routes move and when

items.years_out_basis: An estimate, not a stated date: design, engineering and permitting of about a year and a half, construction starting within six months of that per RIPTA's own packet, and about two years to build.
items.notes: The buses route to the Francis and Gaspee frontage by the State House and the station. Opposition on record: Kennedy Plaza Resilience Coalition; a former board member urged delay pending a service analysis.

items.name: Providence Station renovation
items.where: State of Good Repair and Capacity Project: construction began fall 2024 on a roughly two-year schedule; every official source gives 2026 for completion, and RIDOT said on March 3, 2026 that the work would be complete this year. No completion announcement found as of September 3, 2026. About $30M: $12.5M FRA grant, $9.75M Amtrak, $7.75M RIDOT. Amtrak owns the station.

needs.text: Completion of the current construction phase, stated as 2026 with no date

items.years_out_basis: Stated for 2026 by RIDOT in March 2026; not yet verified.

items.name: Providence Place tax agreement expiry
items.where: The 1996 tax stabilization agreement runs through 2028 (end of fiscal 2027-28). Under it the mall pays about $500,000 a year in property tax and roughly $1 million a year to the city in all; at the fiscal 2027 commercial rate the bill would be $26.8 million on the current $730 million assessment. But the property sold for $133 million, less than a fifth of that assessment, and would be reassessed before its first full bill, so the cliff is smaller than the headline. The sale closed August 20, 2026 with no tax-deal contingency. Paolino says the owners have no immediate plans to seek a new agreement unless a dramatic development proposal warrants one. Brookfield's 2022 proposed 20-year extension at $4.5 million a year never got a council vote.

needs.text: Either a new agreement negotiated with the City Council before 2028, or a reassessment at something near the sale price; the owners say they are not asking for the former yet

items.years_out_basis: The agreement expires in 2028; that is the clock. Whether it is a cliff depends on the reassessment. An estimate.

items.name: The green parcel across from the mall (now the RIPTA hub site)
items.where: It is the same lot. The empty, grassed, state-owned parcel west of Providence Station fronting Francis and Gaspee streets, about 4.4 acres, the PVD Fan Zone during the 2026 World Cup, is the parcel RIPTA's board chose on August 20, 2026 for the new transit center. A separate parcel at 150 Francis Street is owned by Amtrak and was studied earlier; Park Row West, on the other side of the station, was Next Wave's higher-ranked site before the Francis Street lot was picked for its footprint.

needs.text: The RIPTA hub decision: the parcel's only live use is the transit center, so what happens here is what happens there

items.notes: Which lot Liam meant by the green parcel is still his to confirm; if it is this one, the row collapses into the RIPTA hub row and one 'what could be built' item is the site of another.

items.name: Hospital parking lots in the Jewelry District
items.where: Brown University Health holds 4,280 surface spaces including off-site, more than 40 acres of it in the hospital district. The City Plan Commission approved its Institutional Master Plan in May 2026: the main entrance moves to Plain Street, a 500-space garage is built, Plain and Dudley reconnect. While the garage is built, the hospital will park on the Victory Plating site in the Jewelry District. Marathon's separate seven-story garage at 140 Prairie Ave is paused after neighborhood opposition, and its 251 Blackstone St building was cut from six stories to four. The March 2025 CNU charrette's 2,000-unit proposal on consolidated lots is a proposal, not a plan of record; the approved plan says nothing about housing.

needs.text: The Plain Street garage built; until then a Jewelry District lot absorbs displaced parking rather than being freed
Surface parking consolidated into structures before any lot can be built on

items.notes: The lots are not being redeveloped; one is being used harder. Lead time on the lots runs downstream of the garage.

items.name: Kennedy Plaza after the buses
items.where: Tied to the RIPTA move: Kennedy Plaza would go from the system's hub to a stop with reduced Downtown Transit Connector service. No standalone plan for the plaza found beyond the transit change. Kennedy Plaza is City-owned; RIPTA is a tenant there. Paolino, who owns 100 Westminster overlooking it and now the mall, has said publicly he wants the buses out.

items.years_out_basis: An estimate: the plaza changes only when the buses leave, so it runs on the transit center's clock. No plan of its own.
